- Complete source proof text:

```text
Let f(x)=x^2+1∈ℝ[x] and I=⟨f⟩.

(Radicality.) First, f has no real root: for every r∈ℝ we have f(r)=r^2+1>0, so f(r)≠0. Hence f is irreducible in ℝ[x]. Since ℝ[x] is a UFD, an irreducible element is prime; therefore f is prime, hence radical as an element. Using the equivalence that f is radical if and only if the principal ideal ⟨f⟩ is radical, we conclude that I is a radical ideal.

(Zero locus is empty.) By definition, V(I)={ r∈ℝ | ∀ g∈I, g(r)=0 }. If r∈V(I), then since f∈I we must have f(r)=0. But f(r)=r^2+1≠0 for all r∈ℝ, a contradiction. Thus V(x^2+1)=∅.
```

- Source proof / prover notes:
  - For radicality, follow the source route if convenient: show `x^2+1` has no real root, infer irreducibility over `ℝ`, then prime, then the principal ideal is prime and radical. A quotient-based proof may also work if it preserves the same statement.
  - For emptiness, unfold `realAffineZeroLocus`, take a point `r`, use the generator membership `xsqAddOneRealPolynomial ∈ xsqAddOneIdeal`, and reduce to `(Polynomial.X ^ 2 + 1).eval r = r^2 + 1`, contradicting `sq_nonneg r` plus positivity of `1`.
